pageCache.pageTitle: School mission and values - Westminster City School
pageCache.text:
School mission and values
Westminster City School has a long history of educating young people in London.
Our mission
Westminster City School offers exceptional learning opportunities, promoting wisdom, integrity and excellence within an inclusive and compassionate community. Our dynamic Christian foundation and rich heritage help equip each person with the life-skills needed to flourish.
Our values
All members of our School community – students, parents/carers, staff and governors – be they of the Christian faith, of other faiths or of no faith, are bonded by the four values that underpin this purpose:
Wisdom
We nurture wisdom by developing academic habits and skills, emotional intelligence, resilience and creativity in all.
Teach me good judgement and knowledge, for I believe in your commandments. (Psalm 119.66)
Integrity
We foster integrity by encouraging all young people and adults in our community to match words with deeds, fulfil commitments, and take responsibility for their behaviour.
Show yourself in all respects a model of good works, and in your teaching show sincerity, dignity, and sound speech (Titus 2.7)
Compassion
We cultivate compassion by valuing each person in our community and empowering them to share their gifts and aspirations.
I give you a new commandment that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also should love one another. (John 13.34)
Excellence
We develop excellence by ensuring all in our community do their best, take pride in achievements, and are open to change and learning from others.
Whatever you do, do everything for the glory of God. (1 Corinthians 10.31)

pageCache.pageTitle: Statement of British values - Westminster City School
pageCache.text:
Statement of British values
At Westminster City School, we help our young people grow into caring, responsible and tolerant adults, who can make a positive difference to British society and to the wider world.
All British schools are required to promote the fundamental British values of: democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect, and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs. These are values that have come to be accepted throughout the democratic world, helping to create a safe and supportive society.
At Westminster City School, we actively promote British values in the following ways:
Democracy
We encourage students to debate topics of interest and to make a meaningful contribution to our School. Our sixth formers, for example, take on leadership roles and responsibilities, while all pupils and students are regularly consulted (both formally and informally) on how our School may be improved. During national elections, we hold our own mock elections, helping our young people go beyond the classroom to learn more about the British electoral system.
Rule of law
Our School’s sanctions and behaviour policy are well established and shared, while our rewards system creates a positive ethos. As well as rewarding 100 percent attendance and punctuality, we reward work of high quality, work that improves on past achievements, and consistent hard work and service to our local community. Assemblies celebrate achievements, as does our weekly parental bulletin where those achieving a significant number of merits and distinctions are acknowledged. Our annual Celebration of Achievement Evening at Westminster Abbey is an excellent event where achievements are also feted. In addition, our PSHCE curriculum in Year 7 develops an understanding of where the role of law comes from, as well as the positives and negatives of democracy, and the rights and responsibilities that we have as a community.
Individual liberty
Our safe and supportive environment helps students develop self-knowledge, self-confidence and a growth mind set in all areas of school life, including beyond the classroom through participation in our many extra-curricular clubs and activities. Independent learning is encouraged and we offer frequent opportunities for our young people to grow in maturity and independence, particularly as they move towards our Sixth Form.
Mutual respect
Our clear anti-bullying policies emphasise the importance of creating an environment in which all individuals feel safe and valued, while our staff code of conduct ensures staff behave towards each other in an exemplary way, setting a good example. In addition, the language used between staff and students is, at all times, considered vital in showing respect to others. Alongside this, our PSHCE programme in Year 7 enhances our School approach with a unit on healthy friendships, including anti-bullying sessions. Our students revisit this theme in our PSHCE drop down days each year, where guest speakers and organisations (such as Diversity Role Models) deliver sessions that promote equality, diversity and respect.
Tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs
Our students and staff have links to over 100 different nationalities, so we help our young people develop an understanding of, and respect for, their own and other cultures. For example, through our PSHCE and our Religious Studies curriculum, our young people are encouraged to discuss and respect the differences and similarities between people. To further enhance this, organisations like Prevent and Caabu (Council for British and Arab Understanding) deliver sessions at our School as part of our PSHCE curriculum. In addition, all at Westminster City School are encouraged to challenge any prejudicial or discriminatory behaviour. We believe our School ethos and vision, and our curriculum, reflects and promotes British values. With our multi-cultural student and staff body, we ensure the education provided at Westminster City School helps develop our young people into good local, national and global citizens of the future.

pageCache.text:
Welcome
Our Sixth Form prepares young men and women for future study and employment, combining academic excellence with guidance on applying to university, a rich careers programme, a plethora of extra-curricular activities, and strong pastoral support.
We are exceptionally proud of our Sixth Form and our amazing students.
Within our Sixth Form, you'll enjoy more freedom and independence than your previous years in education but our supportive learning environment means you will be guided by highly skilled teachers in small classes, whilst our pastoral support and extra-curricular activities help you develop into confident and independent young men and women. Our facilities include a state-of-the-art Sixth Form study suite and common room, with outdoor space. Our central London location places you in the heart of the capital, within walking distance of the Houses of Parliament, Buckingham Palace and Westminster Abbey. This ensures you can go beyond your A Level subjects by attending workshops or lectures with business leaders, participating in conferences or research programmes at top universities or simply visiting the many museums, galleries, theatres, exhibitions and more that are found across London. Our location has also helped us build strong links with nearby organisations, like Polar Capital, an investment company near our Sixth Form. Thanks to generous funding from Polar Capital, our sixth formers will benefit from a fantastic suite of further support. All students joining our Year 12 will receive a free laptop and those thinking of university study can apply for four generous university bursaries, worth over £20,000 a year, for each year of future university study.
Choosing a sixth form is a major decision, so our webpages and our prospectus provide further information about life in our Sixth Form, while our Vimeo channel contains helpful videos about our A Levels.
Mr O Taufik Director of Sixth Form

pageCache.text:
Welcome
It is my great pleasure to welcome you to Westminster City School. We are a comprehensive school for boys, with a mixed sixth form, in central London, close to Buckingham Palace, the Houses of Parliament and Westminster Abbey. Our founders adopted the motto Unitate Fortior – Strength in Unity. It is a sentiment that is as important to our School today as it was when it first opened in 1877.
Since becoming our school's fifteenth headteacher, I have realised why increasing numbers of young people are going that extra mile to be educated at Westminster City School. There is something very special that permeates our School – I call it the ‘Westminster City Factor’. For me, this factor comprises of a unity of so many strengths. Ours is a school unified by its culture, purpose, character, connections and sense of community.
We draw much from our rich history to ensure that everyone within our School’s multi-faith, multi-cultural and forward-thinking community is equipped with the skills and attributes to succeed in the twenty-first century. We are proud of this diversity which ensures our School is a true reflection of the modern city we live in.
Life at Westminster City School is demanding and rewarding, and enriches all within our proud community. Our School offers exceptional learning opportunities within an inclusive community. Our dynamic Christian foundation and rich heritage help equip each person with the life-skills needed to flourish. I hope your visit to our website gives you a firm sense of our aspiration for all that pass through our doors.
Peter Broughton - Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Alumnus John Olatunji Returns for Black History Month - Latest news - Westminster City School
pageCache.text:
Latest news
Alumnus John Olatunji Returns for Black History Month
Westminster City School welcomed back former student John Olatunji on Tuesday 6 October as part of the school’s Black History Month programme, themed ‘Honouring Our Communities’.
John left Westminster City School 16 years ago and is now Director, Head of Liquidity Sales, Europe, Corporate Banking at Deutsche Bank. Returning to speak to Year 12 students, he reflected on his personal experience from school into banking and challenged students to think not only about how they move forward but also about who they bring with them.
Addressing the students in assembly, he said:
“I was sitting in your seats many years ago, trying to work out where I wanted to get to and more importantly, how I was going to get there.
“When I think about the theme of honouring our communities, for me it is a verb. It is about action. It means remembering the past, showing up in the present and helping to raise the people coming behind you.”
John spoke about the practical steps students can start to take now, including attending insight days, applying for internships and work experience as well as building professional networks early.
One message that was said repeatedly from the beginning to the end of his talk is that success should never be treated as an individual achievement.
“Once you are through a door of opportunity, try to bring people with you to the best of your ability. Every door that has opened for me has been because somebody believed in me.
“Remember to thank the people who have opened doors for you, whether that is your parents, teachers or mentors and then think about how you can do the same for someone else.”
Following his talk to the entire Year 12 cohort, John led a smaller workshop for students interested in banking, finance and corporate careers, giving them the chance to ask more detailed questions about the industry and the routes into it.
Nadah, who joined Westminster City School’s Sixth Form from Kingsdale Secondary School and is studying Economics, Geography and Maths, said:
“John gave me a much clearer idea of the career paths I could pursue and what I should be doing now as a Year 12 student. I am interested in finance, so hearing about networking, work experience and what employers and universities look for was really useful.
“The workshop was even better than I expected because we were able to ask more in-depth questions and get honest answers from someone with a lot of experience in the area I am interested in.”
A big thank you to John for returning to Westminster City School as a guest speaker to start our Black History Month’s programme of activities and reminding all that honouring our community is not just about reflecting on those who came before, but it’s also about using your own progress to help others move forward.

Latest news
Gresham College Oratory Competition 2026
Congratulations to Year 13 student Timothy, who received a certificate in recognition of his oratory and participation in the Gresham College Young Orator of the Year Competition 2026.
Timothy was encouraged to enter the competition by one of his teachers and chose to speak about artificial intelligence. His speech explored the balance between embracing AI as a useful tool and ensuring that it enhances human knowledge and capability rather than replacing it.
Public speaking is something Timothy has developed over several years at Westminster City School through his involvement in the school’s Debate Club.
Speaking about the competition, he said:
“I’ve been taking part in Debate Club at Westminster City School for the past three years and I’ve always enjoyed it. It gives me a chance to use my strengths and to think carefully about both sides of an argument when discussing an issue.
“It was really nice to receive recognition from Gresham College for taking part in the competition, which I very much enjoyed.”
Timothy plans to continue developing these skills and is keen to continue on his public speaking journey during his final the year in Sixth Form. After Year 13, he will consider studying Architecture at either UCL or London Metropolitan University.
Well done to Timothy on this achievement and on representing Westminster City School so confidently!

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 13 Students Spend the Day at Jesus College, University of Cambridge - Latest news - Westminster City School
pageCache.text:
Latest news
Year 13 Students Spend the Day at Jesus College, University of Cambridge
Selected Year 13 students visited Jesus College, University of Cambridge on Wednesday 16 September for a day focused on university study and the Cambridge application process.
Students were able to have a tour of the college and wider university; they also took part in academic taster sessions and worked through areas of the application process including personal statements, interviews and choosing a course and college. They were also able to ask their questions directly to an Admissions Tutor and current Cambridge students.
The academic sessions gave students a taste of the subjects they are considering once they have completed their A Level studies at Westminster City School. Misha, who is interested in studying Law, shared that she enjoyed discovering adverse possession during a Cambridge Law session.
“The Law taster lecture really stood out to me because I was able to explore legal concepts such as adverse possession in Land Law in an academic setting. I also found the support from the student ambassadors around applications and mock interviews really encouraging.”
Misha said the visit had made approaching Law at university level feel less daunting and had given her more confidence in preparing an Oxbridge application.
Ayub, who also went on this trip said that the session exploring the use of data analysis in genetics and biology was the highlight of the day.
“It wasn’t my first time visiting Cambridge, but seeing Jesus College and getting a better idea of university life was really interesting. The visit made me more confident about considering Cambridge and gave me a clearer idea of what to expect from the application process.”
Year 13 student Jagroop, who also returned to Cambridge for a second visit, said:
“Being able to explore Cambridge on the tours allowed me to really envision myself attending the university. The trip has solidified my decision to apply and given me a clearer idea of what studying and living there could be like. I was especially impressed with the amount of encouragement for both extracurricular and academic pursuits for students.”
With university applications now on the minds of Year 13s, the visit gave students another useful opportunity to experience their chosen subjects in a university setting and consider whether the University of Cambridge could be the next step for them.

pageCache.pageTitle: Honouring Our Community – A Service of Re-Dedication - Latest news - Westminster City School
pageCache.text:
Latest news
Honouring Our Community – A Service of Re-Dedication
Westminster City School held its annual Re-Dedication Service at St Margaret’s Church on Thursday 24 September, bringing students and staff together at the start of the new academic year to reflect on the school’s values.
This year’s theme of ‘Honouring Our Community’ was looked at by former student Stephen Appiah Kubi, who attended Westminster City School from 2015 to 2022 and returned to speak about the role the school community played in shaping his ambitions.
Stephen, who is a future trainee solicitor at Clifford Chance, shared his insights on the support and encouragement he received during his time at Westminster City School and on the start of his journey to the University of Oxford where he recently graduated.
“The strength of the Westminster City School community played a huge part in shaping who I am today. I was encouraged to aim high, pushed beyond what I thought I was capable of and supported by staff who believed in me.
“What makes this community special is the way staff, students and alumni support one another. There is an African proverb that says, ‘If you want to go fast, go alone; if you want to go far, go together.’ I think that really reflects Westminster City School and the importance of recognising the strengths of the school.”
The service gave the school community time to think about the year ahead and rededicate itself to the values and expectations that shape daily life at Westminster City School. Students were encouraged by Headteacher, Mr Broughton to stay focused in their studies, have the courage to take on new challenges and remember to uphold the values of Wisdom, Integrity, Compassion and Excellence.
There was also an added sense of eagerness for our Year 7 and Year 12 students, as this was their first visit to St Margaret’s Church as part of the Westminster City School community. During the walk from Palace Street, several Year 12 students mentioned the beauty of the church as they approached.
Once inside, a positive and memorable moment came from our Year 7 students who didn’t hold back or shy away from singing, they sang every hymn with confidence and enthusiasm. Their voices filled St Margaret’s Church and brought a real sense of warmth to the service which was centred on belonging, community and shared purpose.
The occasion was a great way to officially start the new school year, bringing everyone together in one of the places that forms an important part of life at Westminster City School.

pageCache.text:
Careers
At Westminster City School, we prepare all our young people for future employment, with a strong careers education programme from the moment they first join us.
An overview of our careers provision can be found on this page. For more information or to support our careers programme, please contact our School's Career Co-ordinator, Ms Dennis, on telephone 020 7963 6300 or email: k.dennis@wcsch.com.
Careers Education at Westminster City School
Our Careers Programme aims to provide students with opportunities to broaden their horizons, raise aspirations and develop the knowledge and skills needed to make well-informed yet ambitious choices about their future beyond school. It aims to empower students to overcome any social, economic and/or academic barriers to success through meaningful career and workplace experiences and access to individualised support to successfully make the transition to their chosen future pathway.
We are very fortunate to benefit from a fantastic location where we can build a number of partnerships. These include partnerships with:
Polar Capital
School of Hard Knocks
Southwark Schools Learning Partnership Careers Hub
WCS student alumni network
Into University, Cambridge University
Westminster 6F Partnership
Mills & Reeve
Grimshaw
British Red Cross
Medicmentor
Gate One Consulting
Make Architects, amongst more.
Key Stage 3 and 4 Opportunities
All year groups experience assemblies from external speakers about careers and next steps in education. These include talks from Oxbridge Alumni students and speakers for Black History Month. They also experience careers education within subject areas and in PSHCE, participate in careers trips and from extra-curricular clubs which include careers elements. External opportunities are regularly shared with students and their parents/carers.
Year 9 have GCSE options talks and a GCSE options fair. Years 10 and 11 have student and parent/carer talks about post-16 education options, including for our Sixth Form. Year 11s also have a Sixth Form Taster Day and workshops for alternative pathways students. Year 11 students, with their parents/carers are also invited to careers fairs in London.
Students in Years 10, 11 and 12 have a one-to-one careers meeting. We also closely track intended destinations for students in Years 11 and 13 to ensure they are aspirational and suitable for our students.
Opportunities within our Sixth Form
In the Sixth Form we have Pathways Programmes in Finance, Medical Careers, Law, Engineering and Education. These offer bespoke support to groups of students considering these fields. This support includes (but it is not limited to) talks about the industry, external speakers, visits, getting work experience, guidance with university selection and applications, guidance with admission tests and interviews and project work. We also have support for admission tests for STEM students. Our Sixth Form students are fully supported with researching and applying to university or non-university routes. They also experience workshops and participate in an organised work experience week.
We work with Polar Capital to offer a wonderful scholarship programme and careers experience. Click here for more information about PCAS.
Year 7
Our Thinking Ahead programme is ideal for pupils as they transition to secondary school, since it helps pupils explore the value of different curriculum subjects and build understanding of the education system through various interactive workshops. Pupils imagine an alien has landed on Earth, where they have to explain why we go to school and why we study different subjects. Learning outcomes for pupils include:
Year 8
Our Self-awareness programme introduces pupils to the concept of job families. Pupils imagine they are stranded on a deserted island, first identifying the key jobs they need to do to survive and then exploring how these roles evolve to build a functioning society.
Activities completed throughout this programme help pupils develop self-awareness, explore careers and challenge job stereotypes. Learning outcomes for pupils include:
Challenging stereotypes.
Year 9
Our Exploration programme helps pupils make informed choices about how to start taking steps towards their future career path, through a combination of interactive activities and the online Career Investigator tool.
Pupils explore the wide number of careers associated with an industry, debating the links between subject choices, skills and careers. Learning outcomes for pupils include:
Reflecting on their career personalities.
Year 10
Our pupils are introduced to ULAS, an online platform, that allows them to investigate a range of careers options. They build a profile of themselves and record instances where they demonstrated key ‘soft-skills’ required in the workplace.
Pupils are audited according to their careers profile and targeted accordingly with opportunities to hear guest speakers and go on educational visits suited to their career ambitions.
All Year 10 pupils are offered the chance to have an academic or business mentor. These mentors support pupils in preparing for exams and developing revision techniques, as well as starting to work on communication and public speaking skills.
Learning outcomes for pupils include:
Year 11
All our pupils sit a psychometric test which measures, amongst other things, their verbal reasoning, numerical skills and memory. It also explores interests and personality type. Results feed into a one-to-one guidance interview with Level 6 trained careers advisors. Following this interview, all pupils are provided with an action plan. Through practical activities, based on a superhero scenario, our pupils better understand their abilities by exercising key skills and recognising the importance of transferable skills. Learning outcomes for pupils include:
Year 12
Our Year 12 students enjoy hearing from weekly guest speakers, who contribute to our Inspire programme. These speakers, from across the industry spectrum, offer invaluable insights into careers, while letting our students hear about apprenticeships, graduate programmes and school leaver programmes, as well as traditional careers. The aim of our programme is not only to provide practical tips about career pathways but to introduce career options that our students may not previously have thought about.
At the end of Year 12, our students have a guidance interview with a Level 6 trained careers advisor. Results inform applications for their next steps, be it their UCAS application or alternative post 18+ pathways.
There are also be subject-specific opportunities, and students are encouraged to sign up to a range of visits and programmes that include workplace visits and exercises and our School's own innovative pathways programmes.
All in Year 12 are offered the chance to have an academic or business mentor. These mentors support students in CV writing, preparing for job interviews and formulating revision programmes.
Year 13
All our Year 13 students attend our Westminster City School careers fair. Our students are also guided through the UCAS process and provided with the opportunity for careers workshops. These workshops enable them to create a LinkedIn profile, to develop their interview techniques and to refine their CV.

The report recognises that a Westminster City School education provides a strong, stable and robust platform for all our current and future students. It shares the positive impressions that inspectors made during the inspection and sets out how ambitious we are for the school.
Ofsted’s new inspection framework, which is a more robust and rigorous approach, sets out judgements in seven areas. There is no overall judgement but the majority of our judgements were graded at the “strong standard”.

The report was informed by very positive survey responses from staff, students and parents alike. It reflects that our sense of community and Christian values are central to all that we do.
We are incredibly proud that inspectors recognised the many ways that the school has evolved and strengthened since its last Ofsted report. The Governors and the school’s Leadership Team are clear that we are taking the right steps and will continue to provide transformational education in the heart of London.

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 9 Students Join Inner Voices Youth Choir - Latest news - Westminster City School
pageCache.text:
Latest news
Year 9 Students Join Inner Voices Youth Choir
Two Year 9 students from Westminster City School, Christian and Judah, have been invited to join Inner Voices Youth Choir, continuing their musical journey which first started when they joined the school as Year 7 Music Scholars. Inner Voices Youth Choir is a London-based youth choir, directed by Ed Watkins, that brings together young singers from different parts of London, giving them the chance to take part in rehearsals, performances and residential opportunities.
Director of Music at Westminster City School, Ms Chan, has seen the progress of Christian and Judah since Year 7. She said:
“We are really proud of Christian and Judah. They began their musical journeys here as Year 7 Music Scholars, singing in the Chamber Choir and playing in the school orchestra. They have shown real commitment to developing their musical skills and it is wonderful to see that recognised through their selection for Inner Voices Youth Choir.”
The link with Inner Voices also reflects the wider Westminster City School music community. A number of former students are now established members of the choir and some have gone on to support younger singers.
“It is also special to see our alumni, including Temi, who is a longstanding member of Inner Voices, now mentoring younger students who first met through Chamber Choir. It is a great example of how the relationships built at Westminster City School continue outside the classroom and beyond a student's time at school.”
Judah, shared the following:
“When I started at Westminster City School in Year 7 and applied to become a Music Scholar, being selected gave me confidence in my ability as a musician. Joining a choir like Inner Voices is exciting, and I am especially looking forward to the residential trip to York.”
Christian also reflected on how much the scholarship has shaped his experience of music at school. He said:
“I applied for the Music Scholarship because it seemed like a great opportunity. Before becoming a Music Scholar, I never had one-to-one music lessons. Since then, I have had experiences I never would have expected, including performing at Victpria Station and at Raffles London at The OWO. Those opportunities have really helped to develop my understanding of music.
“I’m very grateful to have been selected for Inner Voices Youth Choir. I know it will involve a lot of hard work but I’m really motivated and looking forward to it.”
Congratulations to both students on joining Inner Voices Youth Choir!
The Westminster City School Music Scholarship is open to incoming Year 7 students who show existing musical talent and potential. Successful candidates receive free music tuition and are encouraged to take an active role in the school’s ensembles, choirs and orchestra, with opportunities to develop both their musicianship and leadership.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art Students Explore Stone Carving at St Paul’s Cathedral - Latest news - Westminster City School
pageCache.text:
Latest news
Art Students Explore Stone Carving at St Paul’s Cathedral
As part of Westminster City School’s ongoing enrichment programme, Years 10 and Year 11 Art students had the opportunity to take part in a hands-on creative workshop at St Paul’s Cathedral on Tuesday 15 September.
During the visit, students worked alongside skilled stonemasons from PAYE Stonework & Restoration Ltd, a prestigious specialist contractor currently involved in restoration work at both St Paul’s Cathedral and the Tower of London.
Students were introduced to traditional stonemasonry techniques and had the opportunity to carve stone using specialist hand tools. They also learned more about the skills, training and apprenticeship routes involved in becoming a stonemason, providing them with unique details into a highly skilled heritage craft and potential career pathway.
The day also included a workshop with practising artist and architect Peter Ayres, who guided students through the process of creating small 3D typographic models, allowing them to explore the relationship between art, architecture and design.
Year 11 student Jevaughn said:
“My experience at St Paul’s Cathedral was fantastic and insightful. Learning stone carving has given me a new range of skills that I can use in my Art GCSE and helped me develop my precision and patience. It was quite obvious how passionate the stonemasons were about their work.”
The visit provided students with an opportunity to develop practical artistic skills while learning directly from professionals working within the creative and heritage industries.
Westminster City School would like to thank the stonemasons at PAYE and the Urban Learners community for making the workshop possible and providing students with such an interesting and valuable experience.
